    How the fines work

    Missed pickups are sorted by address and date. The first at an address is free. Each later one is a repeat fine. Under the challenge rule, a miss is chronic when it is the 3rd or later at that address within the last 6 calendar months, counting both ends. Each miss gets one fine, the highest that applies.

    Checked against the notebook

    • This page's fine engine was tested against a pandas version of the notebook's rules on 44 scenarios. All 44 matched exactly.
    • Its calendar-month math matched pandas on all 731 dates in the data, shifted back 1 to 12 months (8,772 checks).
    • The defaults reproduce the notebook: $940,400 under the base rule and $1,420,700 under the challenge rule. Each "Notebook scenarios" button matches its notebook total.

    What the data can't show

    Known gaps push these totals down: complaints that mention misses are left out, whole-street misses only count at the address that called, and 245 missed pickups have no known hauler. A few addresses have no usable map location. The map key says how many, and they still count in the totals.

    Data: the class's hubNashville dataset of 20,226 trash service requests, 17,657 of them missed-pickup requests. Analysis: part1_planning.md (Part 1) and trash_haulers_analysis.ipynb (Parts 2 to 4) in Juan's GitHub submission. Built with Claude as a pair programmer.
